title: Mods panel, 19 performance patches, readable HP/mana
items: New Mods panel: a translucent menu docked to the right edge of the screen with one row per feature, showing its icon, live state and a description when you hover it. Every keyboard shortcut the plugins used is gone - click a row instead. (F6 still belongs to Character Utilities.)

New Performance Patches plugin: 19 independently toggleable patches aimed at the stutter, not the average framerate - caching the line-of-sight raycasts the game fires every frame, replacing sorted projectile targeting with a nearest-target scan, spreading enemy AI decisions across frames instead of bunching them, merging damage numbers through a spatial hash, and coalescing health-bar writes.
Frame-time overlay and a 60-second benchmark that writes a CSV with median, p95, p99 and 1% low, so you can measure a patch instead of guessing. Turn vsync off first or the cap hides the difference.
The HP and mana readouts no longer show scientific notation: 1.035056E+11 now reads 103.5 Billion, and the numbers stop flickering between the two.
Summon All can now dismiss your whole army in one click, and the summon counter row sits above your skill bar instead of the top of the screen.
Write-up on where the game actually spends its frame time, with the measurements and the patches that came out of it, is in docs/blog in the repo.

title: QoL plugin suite v1.1.0 - seven plugins, one download
items: New plugin pack on the Mods page: Combat DPS Meter (F9, real dungeon DPS split by you / each summon / DoTs), Readable Numbers (damage as 510 Billion / 1.2 Trillion instead of digit soup), Advanced Tooltips (affix roll ranges + hover ground loot without picking it up), VFX Reducer (F11, three particle-budget modes for dense-floor FPS), Quick Enhance (Shift+click runs the forge to +max), Mijing Floor Selector (F10, jump floors and raise your unlocked cap), and Summon All.
Each plugin is its own DLL - install only what you want; every one fails soft if a game patch changes something.
All plugin GUIDs and configs now use a neutral custom.* prefix; full source and per-plugin docs live in mods/ in the repo.
Character Utilities by Max remains available from the mods-v1.0.0 release; the suite's Summon All button still embeds into its F6 window.

title: Skill trees, story & Corrupted Realm unlocks, mods page
items: Skill Trees panel in the Save Editor: all 12 class trees plus Divine Favor, laid out with the game's real node positions, icons and connection lines. Left-click adds a point, right-click removes one; point pools and row-unlock gating stay consistent.
Trees follow your character — only your class's tabs are enabled, and Divine Favor unlocks at level 100.
Divine Favor nodes show the English name and icon of the choice you picked; hovering lists all three options with their effects.
Unlock story…: a chapter-by-chapter checklist of all 130 levels, with 💀 marking the 60 boss levels. Applies to every loaded file.
Unlock Corrupted Realm…: pick Normal / Hard / Nightmare / Inferno and a floor — and it unlocks the full story at the same time.
New Mods page: download the in-game F6 menu plugins (Character Utilities by Max + SummonAll) with a 3-step install guide.

Home page redesign: the latest release sits right under the tagline, the three feature cards got icons (Item Library, Save Game Editor, Mods), GitHub moved to the top bar, and a full Release history lives below the cards.
Fixed: empty skill sockets no longer render as "+0 to 0"; one-decimal affix values now format like the game; docs refreshed with diagrams.

title: Build sharing, three-file recompose, click-to-edit tooltips
items: Share build: your character (equipment with rolled affixes + talents) packed into a ~1 KB link that fits a free Discord message; opens read-only at #/build. Nothing touches a server — the payload lives in the link itself.
Three-file recompose: the editor asks for slot_N / _auto / _exit together, warns which are missing, mirrors every edit across the trio, and Download all returns them as a set.

Click-to-edit tooltips: click any value, element name, affix line, socketed skill or the quality word directly in the item tooltip and pick a replacement — the item re-renders instantly (Fire → Poison turns the line green).
Game-faithful affix text: every affix line renders with the game's own wording, extracted from the game code with 100% coverage.
Build id in the top-right corner, so a stale cached version is obvious at a glance.

title: Character-view editor
items: The editor became a character screen: hero strip (name, level, divine favor, gold, playtime), the in-game paper-doll, inventory and Global Chest grids, and a talents panel with search-to-invest.
Item tooltips render from your save's actual rolled values — elemental lines, affixes, DOTs, skill sockets, gem sockets, and set sections with worn/unworn dimming.
Safety: a file is only editable after it re-encodes byte-for-byte identically, and edited saves pass the game's own load checks.

title: First release
items: Item library: 3,725 weapons, armor pieces, accessories, gems, consumables and sets — searchable and filterable, with game-style tooltips and 5,197 extracted icons.
Save editor core: parse, edit and download your saves entirely in the browser. Nothing is uploaded, ever.

The OdinSerializer save format ported to TypeScript with byte-identical round-trips, plus full documentation: the wire format, the save data model, and a BepInEx modding guide crediting Max's Character Utilities.
